lines: Routine check-up with unintentional 10-pound weight loss over 3 months
The patient returns for follow-up of COPD, peripheral arterial disease, and tobacco use disorder.
He has no complaints but mentions recent unintentional weight loss of 10 pounds over the past 3 months.
He denies cough, hemoptysis, fever, or night sweats.
- Peripheral Arterial Disease with intermittent claudication (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
He takes controlled with lisinopril, managed with atorvastatin.
On physical examination, he is afebrile, blood pressure is 132/84 mmHg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute.
Lung auscultation reveals clear breath sounds bilaterally.
A chest X-ray is performed, which shows a solitary, 1.2 cm nodule in the right upper lobe with spiculated margins.
A subsequent CT scan of the chest confirms the presence of the nodule without additional abnormalities.
No previous imaging is available for comparison.

encounters.cc: Increasing difficulty climbing stairs and rising from chair over 3 months with dry mouth and intermittent double vision

lines: Increasing difficulty climbing stairs and rising from chair over 3 months with dry mouth and intermittent double vision

This 70-year-old male with a 40-pack-year smoking history and known COPD, peripheral arterial disease, and age-related macular degeneration presents to Neurology following recent identification of a solitary pulmonary nodule concerning for malignancy.
He reports increasing difficulty climbing stairs and getting up from a chair over the past 3 months.
He also reports dry mouth and occasional double vision which seems to improve with rest.
He denies any bowel or bladder dysfunction.
- Peripheral Arterial Disease with intermittent claudication (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Solitary pulmonary nodule with high suspicion for malignancy (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hypercholesterolemia.
On physical examination, the patient has symmetric proximal muscle weakness, and his deep tendon reflexes are diminished but improve after sustained muscle contraction.
Basic metabolic panel and complete blood count are within normal limits.
Chest X-ray reveals a right hilar mass.
